dominant_strengths: Editor screenshot has authentic syntax-highlight palette with clean inline diagnostic chips that feel native to a modern Rust-built IDE.
Dark chrome with subtle dotted grid backdrop gives the marketing surface a developer-tool gravitas without overwhelming the product imagery.
Tab/file-tree typography is tight, monospaced, and hierarchically legible at small sizes, signaling craft to technical audiences.
dominant_weaknesses: Hero is a static editor screenshot with a lone 'Watch Demo' affordance — no motion, no progressive reveal, no felt sense of the product's speed claim.
Three feature blurbs above are clipped at the top of the frame, breaking the spatial rhythm and leaving the headline-to-product transition awkward.
The pixel-art Zed logo block in the terminal panel feels nostalgic but disconnected from the otherwise austere, modern visual language.
fix_priorities: Replace the static editor still with an autoplaying loop or scroll-driven demo that actually demonstrates GPU-fast editing.
Restore full visibility and consistent vertical rhythm to the three-column feature section so the hero reads as a complete unit.
Reconcile the playful pixel mascot with the rest of the chrome — either lean further into retro motifs or replace with a coherent terminal vignette.
Add a secondary CTA or trust signal near the hero to balance the lone Download button against the marketing narrative.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral polish from the editor capture outpaces behavioral clarity (clipped features, single CTA) and reflective payoff feels thin without motion or narrative.
rationale.intent_fit: It reads convincingly as a devtool landing page, but the 'scroll-500' brief implies scroll-driven storytelling that this static, screenshot-led composition does not deliver.
